title: Maybe an error
reporter_text:
Hi, in the dev set:
```
{'task_id': '2697',
 'question': 'For Belles_cookbook_store in January, if we were to move the fraudulent transactions towards a different Authorization Characteristics Indicator (ACI) by incentivizing users to use a different interaction, what would be the preferred choice considering the lowest possible fees?',
 'answer': 'E:13.57',
 'guidelines': "Answer must be just the selected ACI to incentive and the associated cost rounded to 2 decimals in this format: {card_scheme}:{fee}. If a question does not have a relevant or applicable answer for the task, please respond with 'Not Applicable'",
 'level': 'hard'}
```

Belle's mcc is 5942, however 5942 is not contained in fee's "merchant_category_code". I don't think the answer is 'E:13.57'. It is more likely the answer is: 'Not Applicable'. Could you confirm what the answer is? Also, it is very likely in the guidelines it is not {card_scheme} but {aci} since the answer contains an aci letter.
maintainer_reply:
### Hey Rumen, great to see you contributing to the benchmark!
You’ve raised an interesting point, and I appreciate the attention to detail. What you’re highlighting is actually a common challenge for most LLMs—they often struggle with validating their assumptions about how to operate in this domain.
Indeed, there isn’t a fee explicitly tied to Belle's MCC (5942). However, if you check the [manual](https://huggingface.co/datasets/adyen/DABstep/blob/1a8445286e7e16be350561e0fd269e4ffd4e235e/data/context/manual.md?code=true#L95) (something LLMs frequently overlook), you’ll find this clarification in the fee explanation section:
```
* If a field is set to null, it means that it applies to all possible values of that field. E.g., a null value in "aci" means the rule applies to all possible values of "aci."
```
This means that any fee entry where the MCC field is empty actually applies to all MCCs, not just specific ones. The same logic applies to any other attribute left empty, as outlined in the manual.
Let me know if this makes sense, or if you think there’s another angle worth exploring! 🚀

Best,
Martin

First I would love to thank you for ur solid work and contributions.
When I dealing with the dataset, I ran into some small issues:

Hi, thanks for your usage and feedback. Here is some response to your comments:
1. We intentionally deleted some metadata (the total should be around several hours) since they are either low DNSMOS or some hallucination occurred in the transcribed text. We detect these by using the DNSMOS value and text-based repeat detection.

title: Duplicate samples
reporter_text:
I discovered a potential data quality issue in the MMLU-Pro dataset. When analyzing the test split, I found 316 duplicate rows where all columns (except for 'question_id') contain identical values. This means there are repeated questions with the same content and options

Here's the code I used to detect the duplicates:
import pandas as pd
from datasets import load_dataset
```python
dataset = load_dataset("TIGER-Lab/MMLU-Pro")


def check_duplicates(dataset):
    # Convert the dataset to a pandas DataFrame if it's not already
    if not isinstance(dataset, pd.DataFrame):
        df = pd.DataFrame(dataset)
    else:
        df = dataset
    df['options'] = df['options'].apply(lambda x: str(x))
    columns = df.columns
    columns_without_sample_id = [col for col in columns if col != 'question_id']
    # Check for exact duplicates across all columns
    question_duplicates = df[df.duplicated(subset=columns_without_sample_id, keep=False)]
    print(f"\nRows with duplicate values across all columns except 'question_id': {len(question_duplicates)}")

    question_duplicates = df[df.duplicated(subset=columns, keep=False)]
    print(f"\nRows with duplicate values across all columns: {len(question_duplicates)}")
df = dataset['test'].to_pandas()
check_duplicates(df)
```

Results:

316 duplicate rows when checking all columns except 'question_id'
0 duplicate rows when including 'question_id' in the check

title: Missing important parts of text (at least in 20231101.fr)
reporter_text:
Hello,
And first of all, thanks for that great work, it's awesome to be able to have recent wikipedia dump data in HuggingFace :)

Concerning the quality of the data, I was interested in the French part, and I noticed that a lot of "wikicodes" are ignored, leading to some missing parts in the text, on places where there are important pieces of information in terms of knowledge base.

Here is an illustration:
1. Get the text that corresponds to this page: https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint-Valentin
```python
import dataset 
ds = load_dataset("wikimedia/wikipedia", "20231101.fr")
for sample in ds["train"]:
   if sample['id'] == "10034":
      text = sample["text"]
      break
```
2. Print a part:
```python
start = text.index("Au début du")
end = text.index("Reliques des saints Valentin") + 30
print(text[start:end])
```

This prints:
```
Au début du , Charles d’Orléans fit connaître l'œuvre d'Othon à la cour de France. Il écrivit lui-même plusieurs poèmes
dédiés à la Saint-Valentin. Par la suite, cette tradition se perdit dans le monde latin et .

Reliques des saints Valentin 
```
which corresponds to
![Screenshot from 2023-12-04 18-59-03.png](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/62cd40e0299c0c2e0e4261a4/ARKIjXVIymC4eUk2g7Nzo.png)

We can see that "XVe siècle" is missing in the beginning ("[Au début du ] XVe siècle").
As well as the end of the third sentence ("[le monde latin et ]ne fut réactualisée qu'au XIXe siècle[.]").

In the original Wikipedia dumps, that
maintainer_reply:
Hi, @Jeronymous.

Thanks a lot for reporting. Yes, we are aware of this issue, it is an open problem and quite complex to resolve.

The curly brackets in Wikipedia correspond to what they call "templates" (https://meta.wikimedia.org/wiki/Help:Template), and these can be seen as functions: they are given as input the function name and the input parameters, and they produce a text output. This functions are language dependent: each language Wikipedia has their own templates with different names and functionalities.

So, as a first step, we decided to remove all of them, because they are difficult to parse.

But I agree that we miss important information. It would be great that we could improve this and release a better parsing script in future versions. We are open to suggestions. Ideally, we would like to have all templates "transcluded" in the final document.

Maybe the team from Wikimedia can give some ideas, for example, @isaacj who proposed many of the improvements of the cleaning code.
